paragraphs.text: CapCut, the video editing app owned by ByteDance, announced on October 24, 2026, that a plugin for ChatGPT is on the way. The company presented it at CapCut World, an invitation-only creator event held at the Audrey Irmas Pavilion in Los Angeles, according to ShiftDelete.Net and Portal Publicitário.

In a post on X quoted by both outlets, CapCut said the plugin brings its video editing and generation tools alongside ChatGPT. The idea is that a user begins with an idea in a ChatGPT conversation, the plugin turns it into a video inside that conversation, and the result can then be refined in CapCut.
How the plugin works in the demo

A short promotional video released with the announcement shows a user uploading five soccer clips and asking for a 12 second highlight video. ChatGPT responds with a plan that calls for a vertical 9:16 format, quick cuts timed to the music and bright colors. CapCut's editing timeline then appears next to the chat, with the clips and the music track laid out, and the finished cut ends with a text overlay on a player's celebration, as described by ShiftDelete.Net.

Portal Publicitário reported that the draft can be adjusted after it is generated, for example by shortening scenes, changing the order of clips or swapping visuals. It said the plugin can create videos from text prompts or from clips a user uploads, can change the timeline through plain language instructions, and draws on CapCut's library of effects, transitions and music.

According to ShiftDelete.Net, the draft moves into CapCut's web editor, where the user can make further changes and then share or publish the video. Fuzz, a Malaysian technology site, also reported that drafts made with the plugin can be edited further in CapCut.

ShiftDelete.Net and Portal Publicitário both reported that an open beta is planned for November on mobile, desktop and the web, without an exact date. Portal Publicitário added that the first release will happen outside the United States, with a US launch planned later. Fuzz said CapCut had not given a release date and that it was unclear whether the plugin would be free or paid.

None of the reports included pricing, the ChatGPT plans that will support the plugin or the countries where it will launch first beyond the general description above. Fuzz noted that CapCut had not yet described the full set of functions the plugin will offer.
Los Angeles was the second stop in CapCut's creator event series after Singapore, and a final event is planned for London in November, according to ShiftDelete.Net and Portal Publicitário.

The announcement fits a broader push by OpenAI to turn ChatGPT into a platform for outside services. ShiftDelete.Net noted that services such as Spotify and Canva already work inside ChatGPT conversations.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the plugin targets the slowest part of short video work: turning raw clips and a rough idea into a first cut. If the demo holds up in real use, casual creators could get a usable draft from a description, while still keeping a full editor for the final polish. The reported plan to launch outside the United States first means many US users may have to wait.
The next thing to watch is the November beta: which countries and ChatGPT plans get access first, whether the plugin is free, and how closely real results match the soccer highlight demo.
